questions.question: On current Ubuntu, sshd includes /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf at the top of sshd_config. Why does the lesson name the hardening file 01-hardening.conf?
options: sshd ignores files whose names do not start with a digit
For most options the first value sshd reads wins, so an early file overrides later defaults
The last file read always wins, and 01 is read last
Numbered files are reloaded automatically without a restart
questions.explanation: Drop-ins are read in lexical order and, for most sshd options, the first obtained value is used. Verify the effective result with `sudo sshd -T`.

questions.question: You are about to run `sudo ufw enable` on a remote server with `default deny incoming`. What must you do first?
options: Allow SSH (for example `sudo ufw allow OpenSSH`) so your session is not cut off
questions.explanation: With a default-deny policy and no SSH rule, enabling the firewall blocks your own remote access.

questions.question: In `ss -tulpn` output, a database listens on `127.0.0.1:5432`. What does that mean?
options: It is reachable only from processes on the same machine
It is reachable from the whole internet
It is reachable only over IPv6
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback interface, so only local processes can connect. 0.0.0.0 would mean all interfaces.

questions.question: Which command gives user asha sudo rights on Ubuntu WITHOUT removing her from her other groups?
questions.explanation: -a (append) with -G adds the group. Without -a, usermod replaces the user's supplementary group list.
